lines.text: I had a whistle. It was tin. It was mine.
It fell out somewhere when Deacon stepped on my foot. He said sorry. Not with words.
I'm going to play at the dance. After I find my whistle. After.
I'll keep my eyes on the stubble, Pip. They're nearer the ground than they used to be.
It's in the field somewhere. Over toward the wall. I looked there. I looked everywhere there.
Something glints in the stubble, pressed in deep by a very large hoof. A tin whistle, a little flatter on one side than it started.
One note better than it was, or one worse. We'll let him decide.
Pip takes the whistle in both hands, turns it over, and blows. It makes one note, with great conviction.
You can have this. It's been in my pocket. It's got some pocket on it.
Pip plays his note at Eldwin, then at the ox, then at Eldwin again, in case he missed it.
Mrs. Ness says I can play after the dance. When everyone's gone home. She says that's the best time.
